title: CardCorpus artist
description: One artist's cards in one catalog: every card of it whose credit names them (their id among the card's `artists`), oldest first (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#card-lists). A catalog they have no cards in has no file.

name.description: The name to show them under.

catalog.description: The catalog whose cards these are.

cards.description: Every card of the catalog whose credit names them, oldest first.

cardSummary.title: CardSummary
cardSummary.description: A card as every list gives it: where it is (`$kind`, `set`, `id`, the pointer to it) and what a tile draws from, each field the card's own, whole. A card in its set's file has every one of these, and the rest of its fields.

$kind.description: What the pointer points at: `card`. index.json's `pointers` say where to find it (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#pointers).

id.description: The card's id, unique in its set. Treat it as opaque: it never changes once published.

name.description: The card's name as it prints it, in its language: "リザードン" on a Japanese Charizard. Where no source gives the printed name yet, its English name (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#names).

englishName.description: The card's name in English, on every card, the same as `name` on an English card: "Charizard". What to search and sort by across languages (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#names).

subtitle.description: The smaller name the card prints beside its own, as it prints it, in its language, where it prints one: "Professeur Chen" on a French Professor's Research, "オーキド博士" on a Japanese one. Where we have no printed subtitle, the English one on a card whose `name` is its English one (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#subtitles).

englishSubtitle.description: The smaller name the card prints beside its own, in English, where it prints one: the professor on a Professor's Research ("Professor Oak"), the boss on a Boss's Orders ("Ghetsis"). It says which of the cards sharing a name this is, but isn't part of the name: a deck counts them all as one card. Always one of the card's `characters` (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#subtitles). Our own pages show it joined to the name: "Professor's Research (Professor Oak)".

number.description: Its number as printed ("4/102", "SWSH001"), and that number without its set total.

printed.description: The number as printed, where the card prints one.

short.description: The number without its set total: "4" of "4/102", and the whole number where it prints no total ("SWSH001"). What a tile shows and a sort reads.

rarity.description: Its rarity, as its mark reads (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#rarity).

language.description: The language its text is printed in: its set's, or another where its product held a foreign print (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#foreign-prints). Every card has one.

released.description: When the card first came out, in any of its variants: its own date, or, in a set whose cards came out together, the set's (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#release-dates).

date.description: The date, as precisely as is known: 2001, 2001-09 or 2001-09-22; absent where neither the card's nor the set's is known.

sort.description: Sorts cards oldest first, every list alike: compare as plain strings. An ordering convention, not a date; every card has one.

inferred.description: `true` where the card's date is an estimate: no page dates the card itself, so its year is borrowed from another language's print or worked out from its neighbours, its copyright line or its product, or it takes its set's date, which is one (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#release-dates). Absent otherwise.

credit.description: The credit as printed ("CR CG gangs & K. Hoshiba").

artists.description: The people the credit names, in credit order, each by pointer with the name as this card prints it; a director's credit names no one.

$kind.description: What the pointer points at: `artist`. index.json's `pointers` say where to find it (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#pointers).

name.description: The artist's name as this card prints it.

species.description: The species it shows, each once, in the order the card shows them, each with the forms of it the card shows where that is more than its ordinary form.

$kind.description: What the pointer points at: `species`. index.json's `pointers` say where to find it (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#pointers).

name.description: A copy of the target's own `name`.

forms.description: The forms of the species the card shows, in the card's order, where it shows something other than the species' ordinary form alone (a Gigantamax, a regional form, two forms at once): every form it shows then, the ordinary one included. Usually absent: the card shows the ordinary form alone. One entry on a card of a single other form (a Mega, a Gigantamax, a regional form). Two or more where the card shows several forms of the species, the ordinary one listed with the others where it is among them (Tatsugiri's three: `978`, `978:droopy`, `978:stretchy`).

id.description: The form's id: the dex number, with ":<key>" for a form other than the default ("52", "52:galar"). With the entry's own `id` as `species` it is a form pointer.

name.description: The form's name as this card gives it.

picture.description: The picture to show for the card (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#pictures): `front.image`, and `front.of`, the variant it is a picture of (its default variant, another variant standing in, or, for a reprint with no picture of any variant, its original's); `back`, where its back is unlike the usual one; `oversized` where the card only came as a jumbo or its picture is a jumbo variant's.

front.description: The front: a picture id, and whose picture it is.

of.description: The variant it is a picture of, where that isn't the variant it is on (on a card, always).

$kind.description: What the pointer points at: `variant`. index.json's `pointers` say where to find it (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#pointers).

card.description: The card's id, unique in its set.

id.description: The variant's id, unique among its card's variants.

relation.description: Whose card it is, where not the card's own: `original`, the card a reprint with no picture of its own reprints. Label the picture by it ("the original's picture") without following the card's links.

watermark.description: Whose watermark the picture carries, where it carries one.

back.description: Its back, where that is unlike the usual one.

oversized.description: Present where the card only came as a jumbo or its picture is a jumbo variant's.

defaultVariant.description: The variant that stands for the card where one must (prices, a tile): by id in `variants`. Whose photo the card's picture is can be another variant's: read `picture.front.of` for that.

painting.description: The painting it prints, where another card prints it too. Its file (paintings/{id}.json) holds the card's links: the same card in other languages, the card it reprints and its reprints, and its parallels, with every card they name (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#links).

$kind.description: What the pointer points at: `painting`. index.json's `pointers` say where to find it (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#pointers).

id.description: The painting's own id, which never changes: its first print's English name and a short code, such as `charizard-k3f9`. Where it was first printed is `firstPrint`'s to say, corrected there when research finds an earlier print.
